prompt:
Research the Kubernetes project's official policy on how many minor versions are supported at once and for how long each receives patches. Cite the Kubernetes documentation and quote it.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on the Kubernetes documentation, here is the official policy regarding supported minor versions and patch support duration.

The Kubernetes project maintains support for the three most recent minor releases. Each minor release receives patch support for approximately one year (for versions 1.19 and newer), followed by a two-month maintenance period.

Here are the specific claims supported by the documentation:

SOURCE: https://kubernetes.io/releases/version-skew-policy/ | QUOTE: "The Kubernetes project maintains release branches for the most recent three minor releases (1.37, 1.36, 1.35)." | CLAIM: Three minor versions are supported at once.

SOURCE: https://kubernetes.io/releases/version-skew-policy/ | QUOTE: "Kubernetes 1.19 and newer receive approximately 1 year of patch support." | CLAIM: Each supported minor release receives patch updates for about one year.

SOURCE: https://kubernetes.io/releases/patch-releases/ | QUOTE: "the Kubernetes Community will support active patch release series for a period of roughly fourteen (14) months." | CLAIM: The total support window, including a maintenance period, is about 14 months.

SOURCE: https://kubernetes.io/releases/patch-releases/ | QUOTE: "The first twelve months of this timeframe will be considered the standard period." | CLAIM: The standard period for active patch releases is 12 months.

SOURCE: https://kubernetes.io/releases/patch-releases/ | QUOTE: "the patch release series will enter maintenance mode" for a final two-month period after the standard 12 months. | CLAIM: After one year of standard support, a release enters a two-month maintenance mode.

SOURCE: https://kubernetes.io/releases/patch-releases/ | QUOTE: "At the end of the two-month maintenance mode period, the patch release series will be considered EOL (end of life)..." | CLAIM: The support lifecycle ends after the 14-month period (12 months standard + 2 months maintenance).
